answers.answer: 2 players: 4 Player cards each; 3 players: 3 each; 4 players: 2 each. Remove/set aside the Epidemic cards before dealing (the remaining City and Event cards are shuffled and dealt). Pawns start in Atlanta.
answers.evidence: Setup: deal Player cards; remove Epidemic cards and set aside; place matching pawns in Atlanta.

answers.answer: Put the Infection Rate marker on the leftmost 2 space. Flip 3 cards and place 3 matching cubes in each named city; flip 3 more and place 2 each; flip 3 more and place 1 each. Put all 9 revealed cards face up on the Infection Discard Pile; remaining cards form the Infection Deck.

Use 4 Epidemics for Introductory, 5 for Standard, or 6 for Heroic; remove unused Epidemic cards from the game. Divide remaining Player cards into that many face-down piles, as equal in size as possible; shuffle one Epidemic into each pile; stack piles with smaller piles on the bottom.
answers.evidence: Setup: Prepare the Player Deck; difficulty and three preparation steps.

answers.answer: Take up to 4 actions; you may repeat an action or stop early. Discard action-cost cards to the Player Discard Pile. Then draw 2 Player cards together, resolve Epidemics first and reduce to the hand limit; next Infect Cities. After all three phases, play passes left.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure; Actions; Drawing Player Cards; Hand Limit.

answers.answer: Drive/Ferry: move along a white line to a connected city, no card. Direct Flight: discard the card naming your destination. Charter Flight: discard the card matching your current city to go anywhere. Shuttle Flight: move from a research-station city to any other research-station city, no card. White lines going off one edge wrap to the other edge (example: Sydney and Los Angeles).
answers.evidence: Movement Actions; Special Rules & Edge Cases, ‘Board wrapping.’

answers.answer: Normally, discard the City card matching your current city, take a station from the supply, and place it there. If all 6 are on the board, relocate one from anywhere on the board. If more than 6 stations are supplied, set the extras aside during setup.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, ‘Build a Research Station’; Special Rules, ‘Research station limit.’

answers.answer: One Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen cured color from the city; it removes only 1 cube of an uncured color. Treating each different color takes a separate action. Return removed cubes to the cube supply.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, ‘Treat Disease’; Cure Procedure; removed cubes return to the cube supply.

answers.answer: At any research station, discard 5 City cards of the same disease color (4 for the Scientist) and move that disease’s cure marker to its Cure Indicator. The station city need not match the disease color. Existing cubes remain; cured disease can still receive cubes until eradicated. If no cubes of that color are on the board, it is immediately eradicated and the marker is flipped.
answers.evidence: Other Actions, ‘Discover a Cure’; Cure Procedure.

answers.answer: Give another player in the same city the City card matching that city, or take that card from them. Both players must agree. If the recipient exceeds 7 cards, they immediately discard cards or play Event cards until at most 7.

The Researcher may give any City card from their hand to a player in the same city, on either player’s turn. This exception does not let another player give an arbitrary nonmatching City card to the Researcher.
answers.evidence: Roles, Researcher; Special Rules & Edge Cases, ‘Researcher exception.’

answers.answer: After actions, draw 2 Player cards together. If fewer than 2 cards remain when the draw is needed, the game ends and players lose; discards are not reshuffled.

Resolve the Epidemic in order: increase the Infection Rate marker; draw the bottom Infection card; place 3 matching cubes, adding only enough to reach 3 if the city already has cubes, then trigger an outbreak. With 2 already there, add 1 to reach 3 and outbreak. Discard that Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile; Intensify by reshuffling only the Infection Discard Pile and placing it on top of the Infection Deck. Remove the Epidemic card from the game; do not draw a replacement Player card.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, steps 1–3 and after-resolution rule.

answers.answer: Resolve the first Epidemic completely, then the second completely; Events may be played between them. First resolve any Epidemic cards drawn, then discard cards or play Events until the hand is at most 7.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, two Epidemics; Hand Limit, reduction order.

answers.answer: Flip the top Infection cards, one at a time, equal to the current infection rate. For each, place 1 matching cube unless that disease is eradicated; if the city already has 3 of that color, place no fourth cube and cause an outbreak. A cured but not eradicated disease still receives cubes under these rules. Discard each Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Infecting Cities; Cure Procedure says cured disease still infects until eradication.

answers.answer: An outbreak advances the Outbreaks marker 1 space and spreads 1 cube to each connected city. If a connected city already has 3 of that color, its chain outbreak occurs after the current outbreak resolves and advances the marker again. The first city has already had an outbreak on this Infection card, so no cube is added to it in the chain reaction. Each city can hold up to 3 cubes of each color, not 3 total across colors.

No. An Event cannot be played between drawing an Infection card and resolving it, so Airlift cannot move the Quarantine Specialist before that outbreak. It may be played between Infection cards (the summary permits Events at any time except between drawing and resolving a card). Any player may play it; the player using it chooses its use. It is not an action, and the played Event goes to the Player Discard Pile.
answers.evidence: Event Cards rules; Airlift effect; Infecting Cities resolves cards one at a time.

answers.answer: As an action, take 1 Event card from anywhere in the Player Discard Pile and store it on the Contingency Planner Role card. Storage limit is 1 and it does not count against the hand limit. When played, remove it from the game instead of discarding it.

As an action, Dispatcher may move any pawn to a city with another pawn, or move another player’s pawn as if their own; moving another player’s pawn requires that owner’s agreement. Direct/Charter Flight costs are paid from the Dispatcher’s hand; a Charter card matches the moved pawn’s departure city. Dispatcher may move another pawn but cannot make it Treat Disease or take other nonmovement actions, and cannot use the Operations Expert’s special move.

Win immediately when cures for all 4 diseases are discovered; neither eradication nor a clear board is required. Lose if the Outbreaks marker reaches the last space (8th outbreak), if the needed disease cubes cannot be placed (during Epidemics, outbreaks, or infections), or if a player cannot draw 2 Player cards after their actions.
answers.evidence: Victory; Defeat; Special Rules, ‘Cube supply check.’

answers.answer: Place the board within reach and put the 6 stations and disease cubes nearby, separated by color; place 1 station in Atlanta; set the Outbreaks marker to 0; put all 4 Cure markers vial-side up near the Discovered Cure Indicators. Give each player a Reference card; shuffle Role cards and deal 1 face up to each, put matching pawns in Atlanta, and remove unused Role cards and pawns. First player is the player with the highest-population City card. The summary does not say where extra stations supplied by a box are placed during setup; it says to set them aside.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1–5 and 9; Special Rules, ‘If more than 6 stations supplied.’

answers.answer: The active player decides their actions, even if teammates advise or disagree. Introductory hands are face up; Standard/Heroic hands are private by default, though experienced groups may choose open hands. Anyone may inspect either discard pile at any time.

Removing the last cube before the disease is cured does not eradicate it and has no effect. After it is cured, removing its last cube eradicates it; flip the cure marker to the eradication side. Later normal infections and Epidemics do not place cubes of an eradicated disease.
answers.evidence: Eradication; Cure Procedure; Epidemic and Infecting Cities rules.

answers.answer: Place 3 cubes in the city (which has zero), causing no outbreak merely for reaching 3. Discard the Infection card to the Infection Discard Pile before Intensify.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, Infect step: place 3 cubes; outbreak only if the city already has cubes of that color, then discard card.

answers.answer: Increase still occurs; the card is drawn and cube placement is skipped because the disease is eradicated; the Infection card is discarded to the Infection Discard Pile; Intensify still reshuffles only that discard pile onto the top of the Infection Deck.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards: Increase, Infect ‘unless eradicated’ and discard, then Intensify.

answers.answer: The first Intensify empties the Infection Discard Pile after shuffling it onto the Infection Deck. The second bottom Infection card is then the only card in the discard pile for the second Intensify; it is shuffled and put on top. With zero cubes in its city, the second Epidemic puts 3 matching cubes there, and that city’s card is drawn first during normal Infections and causes an outbreak.
answers.evidence: Epidemic Cards, ‘If 2 Epidemic cards are drawn at once’ paragraph.

answers.answer: The Scientist needs 4 City cards of the same color instead of 5. The cure still requires being at any research station; the cards must match the disease color, while the station city itself need not.
As an action, Operations Expert builds a research station in their current city. No City card is needed, used, or discarded.
Once per turn, as an action, Operations Expert may move from a research station to any city by discarding any City card.
The Medic’s Treat Disease action removes all cubes of one chosen color from the city. The summary says one color per Treat Disease action; it does not remove multiple colors with that one action.

When the cure is discovered, remove all cubes of that cured color from the city where the Medic is already present immediately, without an action. When the Medic later enters another city with cubes of that cured disease via Dispatcher or Airlift, remove all those cubes automatically, also with no action needed.
The Medic prevents placement and outbreaks of cured diseases in the city the Medic occupies. This does not protect adjacent cities or uncured diseases.
Quarantine Specialist prevents placements and outbreaks of every disease color in their current city and all connected cities. The ability does not affect cubes placed during setup.

Resilient Population removes any 1 Infection card from the Infection Discard Pile from the game. It may be played between an Epidemic’s Infect and Intensify steps, so it may remove the card just discarded during that Epidemic before Intensify shuffles the pile.
One Quiet Night skips the next Infect Cities step and no Infection cards are flipped for that skipped step. It does not skip an Epidemic’s Infect step.
answers.evidence: Event Cards, One Quiet Night effect.

answers.answer: Airlift moves any 1 pawn to any city. If it is another player’s pawn, get that player’s permission.

Only Player cards count toward the 7-card limit. Role cards and Reference cards do not count; a stored Contingency Planner Event on the Role card does not count either. Reduce a hand of 9 by discarding cards or playing Event cards until it is at most 7; if Epidemic cards were just drawn, resolve them first.
Government Grant places a research station in any city, regardless of the player’s location, with no card discard needed.
Forecast lets you draw, view, and rearrange the top 6 cards of the Infection Deck, then put them back on top of that deck.
